facts.text: Bitcoin protocol and ecosystem expert covering base-layer mechanics, network upgrades, and the L2/metaprotocol frontier. Owns: UTXO model, coin selection algorithms; transaction structure (txid vs wtxid, weight/vbytes, implicit-fee derivation); Bitcoin Script and address formats (P2PKH, P2SH, P2WPKH, P2WSH, P2TR, multisig, CLTV/CSV timelocks, bech32/bech32m encoding); block and header structure, Merkle roots; PoW mining, difficulty retargeting, the halving schedule and 21M cap; mempool and fee mechanics (sat/vByte, RBF, CPFP, TRUC/BIP-431); soft-fork history (SegWit, Taproot/Schnorr/MAST) and activation mechanisms; Lightning Network (channel construction, HTLCs, routing, BOLT specifications); ordinals, BRC-20, Runes; BitVM and the Bitcoin-L2 landscape (sidechains, drivechains, covenants, Babylon shared security); full nodes, wallets, UTXO-vs-account model tradeoffs. Route consensus theory to distributed-systems-consensus, cryptography math to blockchain-crypto-primitives, tokenomics to blockchain-economics.
Explaining why a Bitcoin transaction's fee is calculated in sat/vByte rather than a flat fee, and why weight or vbytes, not raw byte count, determines that cost after SegWit.
